Respond from the same assigned ethical framework to the supplied opposing complaint about your saved argument. The source is unchanged; the prior reply and objection are fallible attributed arguments, not new facts or authoritative verdicts. You may retain, qualify or change your preference. A changed choice earns no credit by itself. Give a substantive answer, not a declaration that the objection has been resolved. Separate source facts, normative commitments and conditional assumptions. Do not invent empirical magnitudes, people's knowledge or consent to make an argument work. A conditional preference is useful; mere uncertainty is not an instruction to abstain. Self-reported ANSWERED is not ledger acceptance or moral proof. original_quote fields must match a contiguous span at original_path in the saved argument; source_quotes must match the exact source. Keep the final conclusion, its status and remaining objection consistent. Do not reconstruct the entire world or argument graph.
First restate the disadvantaged person's actual complaint fairly, including what they lose under your recommendation and what the feasible alternative would offer them. Concede what is true or morally serious about it. Identify the exact priority premise your answer must defend. Then answer WHY the complainant has reason to accept that priority despite their own burden; repeating your preferred principle or pointing out benefits to a different person is not yet that explanation. Compare the strongest countercomplaint to the alternative and explain which consideration makes a difference. If you rely on numbers, explain why counting is licensed by your framework; if you rely on consent or an assurance, explain its force and limits. Acknowledge what your proposed rule asks the losing person to bear and what remains objectionable after your answer. If you cannot defend the comparative premise, revise the inferential claim and the strength of the conclusion, not just its confidence label. State the strongest useful conclusion that survives. Do not force agreement, a winner, or an automatic priority of imposition over omission, promise over rescue, or rescue effectiveness over assurance.
In factual_review cite an exact quote and JSON pointer in the named origin: PRIOR_ARGUMENT means prior_argument; ASSIGNED_COMPLAINT means assigned_complaint (including raw_assignment); CONSEQUENCE_RECORD means consequence_record when provided. source_quotes are exact contiguous source substrings, without added quotation marks. SUPPORTED is your proposed support assessment, not certification. CONTRADICTED, NOT_ESTABLISHED, NORMATIVE_NOT_FACT and CONDITIONAL are distinct. Keep corrected_statement faithful even when the target is morally serious. Record row IDs only if a consequence record is supplied. Give the normative warrant, its justification and its limits separately from factual corrections.
Before defending your conclusion, compare the assigned complaint and your own saved reasoning against the source and the person-by-option consequence_record. The record is a projection of FALLIBLE model annotations, not an admitted world or a semantic oracle. Exact source text takes priority over every paraphrase. Correct factual errors in either side, and distinguish contradictions from claims that are simply not established. Unsupported severity, knowledge, reliance, institutional entitlement or assent must not become facts. Consent may change a complaint's warrant without removing the physical or financial loss. Distinguish the actual assurance and its wording from a future policy that could qualify assurances. Do not retroactively insert such a qualification. For every quantitative comparison keep the same identified person, option, endpoint, unit and conditional probability. A risk PRESENT under both options can change in magnitude. A recipient's probability is not everyone's probability; do not replace identified people with an unstated identity lottery. Distinguish guaranteed outcomes from possible outcomes. Do not erase a complaint because one factual premise needs correction: restate the strongest objection that survives. Then defend the NORMATIVE warrant for your comparative priority, including why the disadvantaged person should accept it and its strongest counterreason. Neither the matrix, a number, a count of complainants nor the name of a theory supplies this warrant. Separate a justification for this actual choice from a proposed future policy or a hypothetical boundary test. If a warrant remains contestable, retain that objection and calibrate the inferential conclusion itself, not merely a confidence label. No choice is prescribed by the record or by the critic.
